t: You're in Myddelton Square, the largest square in the Clerkenwell part of Islington. It's a residential garden square, built in the 1820s and 1830s, with a playground and plenty of trees. Look at the houses: Georgian, in exposed brick, with high-ceilinged ground and first floors. In the middle stands a large Gothic Revival church. Some consider this the finest and most cohesive square on the New River Estate. Alfred Bertram Soltau, a medical scholar and army physician who lived from 1876 to 1930, was born here.
